Texmaco Rail and Engineering Ltd Concall Summary (Q2 FY27, 11 November 2026) #TEXRAIL

🟡 Management Guidance: 
Management expects the company to deliver better results in the coming quarters, with a stronger rebound in the second half of FY27. The approximately ₹10,000 crore order book is expected to be executed over the coming periods, with freight rolling stock orders scheduled for execution over the next 10 quarters. Around ₹8,000 crore of freight rolling stock orders and ₹3,000 crore to ₹3,500 crore of infrastructure and component orders are expected to be executable during the current and next financial years. The South African turnkey order, covering wagons and locomotives, is scheduled for delivery during FY28 and one additional quarter, followed by a 15-year maintenance commitment. Revenue from this order is expected to begin from FY28, not H2 FY27. Foundry production is expected to reach at least 35,000 to 40,000 metric tonnes, with 25% to 30% coming from exports. Management has earmarked approximately ₹200 crore of capex for different purposes and has completed around 40% of its planned capex for the current year. It expects to fund growth and maintenance capex through internal operational surpluses, without requiring additional debt in the short term. The longer-term Vision 2030 ambition is to build a ₹9,000 crore to ₹10,000 crore revenue business, with ₹4,000 crore to ₹5,000 crore from core businesses and the balance from diversification.

🟢 Green Alert: Standalone revenue from operations increased 15% QoQ to approximately ₹863 crore, compared with ₹753 crore in Q1 FY27. EBITDA stood at ₹88 crore, with a margin of 10.2%, while profit was ₹36 crore. The company delivered 1,106 wagons during the quarter and produced 6,468 metric tonnes from its foundry. All three divisions recorded sequential revenue growth. Rail infrastructure grew approximately 41% to 42% QoQ, while electrical infrastructure grew 38% QoQ. Freight cars contributed 62.3% of standalone turnover, down from 68.8% in Q1 and 74.7% in the corresponding quarter last year, showing improving diversification. Infrastructure and other businesses now contribute approximately 37% of turnover compared with 25% last year. Export orders have increased to 54% of the order book from 9% YoY, while private and export customers together account for approximately 80% to 85% of the core freight rolling stock order book. The electrical business reached approximately ₹250 crore of revenue in one quarter, with an order backlog of around ₹1,600 crore executable over the current financial year and the next four quarters. Foundry capacity has expanded to 60,000 metric tonnes, with management expecting significant export growth. CRISIL upgraded the company's long-term rating from A to A+, and the company continues to reduce debt.

🔴 Red Alert: Revenue remained approximately 31% lower YoY, with Q2 FY26 revenue of around ₹1,250 crore compared with approximately ₹860 crore in Q2 FY27. The decline was primarily due to significantly lower Indian Railways wagon orders. EBITDA margin also declined sequentially from 10.8% to 10.2%, although management stated that the previous quarter benefited from non-recurring other income and that adjusted EBITDA margin was approximately 70 basis points higher in Q2. The company has made a substantial provision of approximately ₹700 crore, which management described as a risk-mitigation measure arising from geopolitical uncertainties. However, management did not explain the detailed composition during the call and referred investors to the earlier published clarification. This remains an important point to independently examine. Private and export orders involve different wagon designs, supply chains and execution requirements, so their production volumes may not match the historical volumes of standard Indian Railways commodity wagons. The South African opportunity also requires setting up a facility in South Africa for maintenance and further business development, creating additional execution and capital requirements. The proposed wheel JV, RVNL JV and NYMWAG-related opportunities are still at different stages of development, with timelines and commercial contributions not yet clearly established. Management also did not provide a detailed multi-year capex and debt forecast.

🔵 Blue Alert: Texmaco 2.0 is focused on strengthening its core freight rolling stock and foundry businesses, expanding into railway adjacencies and increasing exports. The South African opportunity is a major international growth driver, involving approximately ₹4,000 crore of earlier orders and a subsequent ₹1,300 crore locomotive order. The turnkey contract includes wagons, locomotives and long-term maintenance, with locomotive manufacturing participation from India and a planned South African facility. The company is also developing its wheel business through a proposed JV, targeting a broader product range aligned with heavy-haul and high-speed rail requirements. Its NYMWAG JV plant is almost production-ready and has received initial RDSO G-105 certification, with prototype manufacturing dependent on receiving an initial order from Indian Railways. The RVNL JV is waiting for suitable tenders, with management expecting a potential opportunity within FY27. The electrical infrastructure business is another major diversification opportunity, with participation in various tenders linked to power transmission and grid expansion. The company has also entered the defence business, while EPC has turned profitable and electrical contracting is performing well. Management intends to evaluate acquisitions and new opportunities based on commercial readiness, technology, capital requirements and expected returns, with a stated preference for businesses that generate earnings from day one.

🧠 Deep Insight: The most important change at Texmaco is the transformation of its order book from heavy dependence on Indian Railways towards private customers and exports. Earlier, railway contracts accounted for approximately 90% to 95% of orders, whereas management now indicates that private and export business represents around 80% to 85% of the core freight rolling stock order book. This reduces customer concentration risk and creates access to potentially higher-margin international business. However, the transition also means that investors should not judge performance only by wagon delivery volumes, because specialised private and export orders have different production requirements and execution cycles. The current quarter shows improving sequential momentum, particularly in electrical infrastructure and rail infrastructure, but the YoY revenue decline highlights that the recovery is not yet fully established. Another important distinction is that the ₹10,000 crore revenue ambition is not simply an expansion of the existing wagon business. Management wants the core business to contribute ₹4,000 crore to ₹5,000 crore, with the remaining ₹5,000 crore to ₹6,000 crore coming from adjacencies and newer businesses such as passenger mobility, defence and renewables. This is a significant diversification ambition, but several initiatives are still at the development or tender stage. The ₹700 crore provision also deserves careful scrutiny before assuming that future export profitability will translate directly into reported earnings. The central investment thesis is that Texmaco is attempting to evolve from a railway wagon manufacturer into a diversified railway engineering and infrastructure company, with exports, electrical infrastructure and new technology partnerships driving its next growth phase. Investors should monitor quarterly revenue recovery, EBITDA margins, conversion of the ₹10,000 crore order book, South African order execution, the ₹700 crore provision, working capital and the commercial progress of its new JVs.
